newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Sydney Swans football operations manager Rob Snowdon has been asked to make a written statement to the Australian Football League over claims by Tony McGuinness that Sydney had undertaken to nominate him in Tuesday's pre-season draft. If this is the case Sydney could face draft-tampering charges. Page 22.

The Commonwealth Bank yesterday announced a three-year netball sponsorship package believed to be worth more than A$1.5 million annually. In return the National Netball League will be renamed the Commonwealth Bank Trophy. Page 22.

Tim Sheens has been named New South Wales coach for Super League's tri-series involving Queensland and New Zealand. Sheens indicated he would like open games and a more liberal approach from Super League referees. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian cricket team defeated South African local team Boland in Paarl, South Africa by 50 runs in a one-day match. Australia scored 319 runs off their 50 overs with Boland managing 269 in reply. Page 47.

Australian walker Kerry Saxby-Junna is on track with her Sydney Olympic training despite being 19 weeks pregnant. Saxby-Junna will concentrate on training to November after the July birth and is expecting to compete in the 1998 Commonwealth Games. Page 46

Lucy Tyler-Sharman will be permitted to ride in the banned "superman" riding style, at the Australian cycling championships in Launceston, Tasmania next month. Tyler-Sharman will be riding against arch-rival Kathy Watt, who has declined legal advice to us an injunction to prevent Tyler-Sharman riding in the position. Page 46.
THE AGE

Up and coming Australian hurdler Kyle Vander-Kuyp will line up against three of the world's fastest six hurdlers ever on his home track at the Melbourne grand prix meeting tonight. Vander-Kuyp will race against Roger Kingdom (equal 2nd), Jack Pierce (4th)and Tony Jarrett (6th) in the 110 metre race. Page B8.

The Australian Football League has prevented a damaging pay dispute with umpires by signing all listed umpires to new standard contracts. The contracts are for between one and three years, with top umpires earning up A$85,000. Page B8.

Tonight's big meet of the year, the Nike Classic, will be crucial for Australian 400 metre runner Cathy Freeman in her preparation for the world championships in August. Freeman has been battling major changes in her personal life and put in a lacklustre erformances at the Hobart grand prix. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

Triple Commonwealth sprint cycling champion Gary Neiwand last night confirmed he was drug tested at a recent meeting in New Zealand. Neiwand informed the Australian Institute of Sport and the Australian Cycling Federation of the test, but said a story that he may have returned a positive test due to taking banned flu medication was incorrect. Page 86.

The Soccer Players Union has recommended Collingwood Warriors players resume training and playing while a grievance has been filed under the collective agreement between the union and Soccer Australia. The Union is seeking immediate free releases for Warrors players. Page 77.

Australia beat New Zealand yesterday in the Rosebowl women's cricket series to take a 2-1 series lead. Australia were 8 wickets for 190 runs after 50 overs with New Zealand making 179 runs in reply. Page 79.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Super League may move its struggling Western Reds team from Western Australia to Melbourne in a bid to establish a franchise in the lucrative sports market there next year. Such a move would increase speculation of a Super League grand final in Melbourne.Page 80.

Australian golfer Brett Ogle will use a state-of-the-art broomstick chipper when he plays the first round of the A$450,000 Canon Challenge at Terrey Hills today. The chipper, believed to be the world's first of its kind will be used for pitch and run shot from 30 yards. Page 80.

Australian sprinter Melinda Gainsford-Taylor may be sidelined from tonight's Melbourne Grand Prix with a severe case of conjunctivitis in both eyes. Coach Jackie Byrnes forced the world indoor 200m champion to abandon her Tuesday night training session beause of the eye infection and headaches. Page 79.
